title: Price Theory: Demand and Supply
summary: The laws of demand and supply, demand and supply curves, factors that shift them, and how the equilibrium price is set in a market.

notes.text: The quantity of a good or service that consumers are **willing and able** to buy at different prices during a certain period.

notes.label: Law of demand
notes.text: When the price of a good **rises**, the quantity demanded **falls**; when the price **falls**, the quantity demanded **rises** (if all other things stay the same). Price and quantity demanded move in **opposite** directions.

notes.caption: Demand schedule for bread in a town (per day)

notes.text: Plotted on a graph with **price on the vertical axis** and **quantity on the horizontal axis**, the **demand curve** slopes **downwards** from left to right.
Factors that change demand (shift the curve)

items: **Income**: higher incomes increase demand for most goods.
**Tastes and fashion**: popular items are in greater demand.
**Prices of related goods**: if the price of butter rises, demand for margarine (a substitute) increases.

notes.text: The quantity of a good or service that producers are **willing and able** to offer for sale at different prices during a certain period.

notes.label: Law of supply
notes.text: When the price **rises**, producers supply **more** (it is more profitable); when the price **falls**, they supply **less**. Price and quantity supplied move in the **same** direction, so the **supply curve slopes upwards**.

items: **Factors that change supply**: costs of production (wages, raw materials, fuel), technology, the weather (for farm products), the number of producers, taxes and subsidies.

notes.caption: Demand and supply schedule for bread

notes.text: The price at which the quantity demanded equals the quantity supplied. On a graph it is where the demand and supply curves cross.

items: **Surplus** (excess supply): at prices above equilibrium, more is supplied than demanded. Sellers lower prices to get rid of stock.
**Shortage** (excess demand): at prices below equilibrium, more is demanded than supplied. Buyers compete and the price rises.
In this way the **price mechanism** moves the market towards equilibrium.

notes.title: A change in the market
notes.problem: A drought destroys much of the maize crop. What happens to the price of maize meal?
steps: Supply decreases (the supply curve shifts left).
At the old price there is now a shortage.
The price rises until a new, higher equilibrium is reached.
notes.answer: The price rises and less is sold.

notes.title: Finding equilibrium from a table
notes.problem: At R10, buyers want 80 and sellers offer 40. At R15, buyers want 60 and sellers offer 60. At R20, buyers want 40 and sellers offer 80. Find the equilibrium, and describe the market at R20.
steps: Equilibrium is where quantity demanded equals quantity supplied.
This happens at R15, with 60 units.
At R20, sellers offer 80 but buyers want only 40, leaving 40 units unsold.
That surplus pushes the price back down.
notes.answer: Equilibrium is R15 and 60 units. At R20 there is a surplus of 40 units.
